front: A single-phase load operates at \(V = 100\angle{0^{\circ}}\ \text{V rms}\) and draws current \(I = (3 - 4j)\ \text{A rms}\) into the load. Determine the complex power \(S\) absorbed, and give \(P\) and \(Q\).
explanation: Step 1: Complex power \(S = V I^{*}\). Step 2: The conjugate is \(I^{*} = (3 + 4j)\ \text{A}\). Step 3: \(S = (100)(3 + 4j) = 300 + 400j\ \text{VA}\), so \(P = 300\ \text{W}\) and \(Q = 400\ \text{VAR}\), inductive since \(I\) lags \(V\).

front: A single-phase load absorbs \(P = 6\ \text{kW}\) at a power factor of \(0.8\) lagging from a \(240\ \text{V rms}\) source. Find the apparent power \(S\), the reactive power \(Q\), and the rms line current \(I\).

A \(60\ \text{Hz}\) single-phase load draws \(6\ \text{kW}\) at \(0.6\) power factor lagging. What reactive power must a parallel capacitor bank supply to raise the overall power factor to \(0.8\) lagging?

A balanced wye-connected load has a per-phase impedance \(Z = 8 + 6j\ \Omega\) and is supplied by a \(208\ \text{V}\) (line-to-line) three-phase source. Determine the total real power absorbed by the load.
explanation: Step 1: Phase voltage \(V_\phi = 208/\sqrt{3} \approx 120\ \text{V}\). Step 2: \(|Z| = \sqrt{8^{2} + 6^{2}} = 10\ \Omega\), so \(I_\phi = 120/10 = 12\ \text{A}\). Step 3: \(P = 3 I_\phi^{2} R = 3(12)^{2}(8) = 3456\ \text{W} \approx 3.46\ \text{kW}\).

front: A balanced delta-connected load with per-phase impedance \(Z = 12 + 9j\ \Omega\) is connected to a \(208\ \text{V}\) three-phase line. Find the magnitude of the line current.
explanation: Step 1: In a delta load the phase voltage equals the line voltage, \(208\ \text{V}\). Step 2: \(|Z| = \sqrt{12^{2} + 9^{2}} = 15\ \Omega\), so \(I_\phi = 208/15 \approx 13.87\ \text{A}\). Step 3: \(I_L = \sqrt{3}\,I_\phi \approx \sqrt{3}(13.87) \approx 24\ \text{A}\).

front: A balanced three-phase load draws a line current of \(20\ \text{A}\) at a line voltage of \(480\ \text{V}\) with a power factor of \(0.85\) lagging. Determine the total real power delivered.
explanation: Step 1: Total three-phase real power \(P = \sqrt{3}\,V_L I_L \cos\theta\). Step 2: \(P = \sqrt{3}(480)(20)(0.85)\). Step 3: \(P \approx 14{,}130\ \text{W} \approx 14.1\ \text{kW}\).

front: An ideal single-phase transformer has a turns ratio \(N_1{:}N_2 = 10{:}1\). Its primary is connected to \(2400\ \text{V}\) and its secondary feeds a \(12\ \Omega\) resistive load. Find the secondary voltage, the secondary current, and the primary current.
An ideal transformer has a turns ratio \(a = N_1/N_2 = 5\). A \(4\ \Omega\) impedance is connected across the secondary. What impedance is seen looking into the primary?
explanation: Step 1: Impedance reflects by the square of the turns ratio, \(Z_1 = a^{2} Z_2\). Step 2: \(Z_1 = (5)^{2}(4) = 100\ \Omega\).

front: A \(24\ \text{kVA}\), \(2400/240\ \text{V}\) single-phase transformer operates at rated load. Find the rated primary and secondary currents.
In per-unit analysis a system uses a base apparent power \(S_\text{base} = 10\ \text{MVA}\) and a base voltage \(V_\text{base} = 10\ \text{kV}\). Determine the base impedance.

A generator reactance is \(0.20\ \text{pu}\) on its nameplate base of \(50\ \text{MVA}\), \(13.8\ \text{kV}\). Express this reactance in per-unit on a new base of \(100\ \text{MVA}\), \(13.8\ \text{kV}\).
explanation: Step 1: \(X_\text{new} = X_\text{old}\left(\dfrac{S_\text{new}}{S_\text{old}}\right)\left(\dfrac{V_\text{old}}{V_\text{new}}\right)^{2}\). Step 2: The voltage base is unchanged, so \(X_\text{new} = 0.20(100/50) = 0.40\ \text{pu}\).

front: A capacitor with a reactance of \(20\ \Omega\) is connected across a \(240\ \text{V rms}\) single-phase supply. How much reactive power does it supply?
explanation: Step 1: For a purely reactive element \(Q = V^{2}/X\). Step 2: \(Q = 240^{2}/20 = 57{,}600/20 = 2880\ \text{VAR} = 2.88\ \text{kVAR}\) (supplied).

front: A load has voltage \(v(t) = 170\cos(377t)\ \text{V}\) and current \(i(t) = 10\cos(377t - 60^{\circ})\ \text{A}\). Find the average (real) power absorbed by the load.
A single-phase load has an apparent power of \(25\ \text{kVA}\) and a real power of \(20\ \text{kW}\). Determine the reactive power and the power factor.

A single-phase source feeds two parallel loads: Load 1 absorbs \(10\ \text{kW}\) at unity power factor, and Load 2 absorbs \(10\ \text{kVAR}\) (purely inductive, drawing \(0\ \text{W}\)). Find the total apparent power and the overall power factor.
explanation: Step 1: Add real and reactive parts: \(P = 10\ \text{kW}\), \(Q = 10\ \text{kVAR}\). Step 2: \(S = \sqrt{P^{2} + Q^{2}} = \sqrt{10^{2} + 10^{2}} \approx 14.1\ \text{kVA}\). Step 3: \(\text{pf} = P/S = 10/14.1 \approx 0.71\) lagging.

front: A \(4\)-pole three-phase induction motor is supplied at \(60\ \text{Hz}\) and runs at \(1746\ \text{rpm}\). Determine the synchronous speed and the slip.
